v.q: What does a Resilience4j decorator do?
o: Wraps a call and adds one behaviour such as a breaker, retry or limit
Rewrites the called service so it never fails
Replaces the HTTP client with a faster one
Moves the call to a message queue automatically
v.w: Each decorator is independent and small, and they can be stacked.

v.q: Why does each dependency get its own named instance?
o: So one failing dependency never trips the breaker or fills the bulkhead of another
Because names are required by the JVM
Because instances share one global failure count by design
v.w: State lives per instance in a registry, for example cardService and ledger.

v.q: Which exception does an open circuit breaker throw?
v.w: The call is rejected at once without reaching the dependency.

v.q: What happens in the HALF_OPEN state?
o: A limited number of trial calls decide whether to close or open again
All calls are rejected until restart
Every call is retried three times
The breaker is disabled and records nothing
v.w: Enough successes close it, failures open it again.

v.q: A low-traffic service never opens its breaker with default settings. What is the likely reason?
o: minimumNumberOfCalls defaults to 100, so the failure rate is not evaluated earlier
Breakers only work with thread-pool bulkheads
The sliding window is time based by default
v.w: Set a realistic minimum, for example 10 with a window of 20.

v.q: What does minimumNumberOfCalls control?
o: How many calls must be recorded before the failure rate is evaluated
How many calls may run at once
How long the breaker stays open
v.w: Without enough calls the rate would be meaningless.

v.q: What is the difference between COUNT_BASED and TIME_BASED windows?
o: Count based keeps the last N calls, time based keeps the calls of the last N seconds
Count based is for retries, time based for bulkheads
There is no difference apart from the name
v.w: Time based lets old failures age out, which suits bursty traffic.

v.q: Which window setting suits steady traffic where each call matters equally?
o: Time based with a one second window
Neither: windows are for retries only
v.w: Count based reacts to the number of calls, not their age.

v.q: Which outcome should normally NOT count as a breaker failure?
o: A business exception such as InsufficientFundsException
v.w: The dependency answered correctly. Use ignoreExceptions.

v.q: A dependency answers every call after 8 seconds and never errors. Which setting opens the breaker?
v.w: Slow calls count even when they succeed.

v.q: What does maxAttempts: 3 mean?
o: Three calls in total: the first and two retries
Three retries after the first call
v.w: The first call counts as an attempt.

v.q: Which operations are safe to retry?
o: Idempotent ones, or ones sent with an idempotency key
Only calls made inside a transaction
v.w: A retried payment without an idempotency key can charge twice.

v.q: Why add randomized wait (jitter) to retries?
o: So many callers do not retry at the same moments and cause a retry storm
v.w: Exponential backoff spreads attempts out and jitter desynchronises them.

v.q: What should Retry not retry when the breaker is open?
v.w: The next attempt would be rejected immediately too, so add it to ignore-exceptions.

v.q: What is the default order of the annotations, outermost first?
v.w: Retry wraps the breaker so every attempt is recorded.

v.q: In the Decorators builder, which decorator is outermost?
o: The one with the shortest name
v.w: Each with... call wraps what exists so far.

v.q: Which bulkhead keeps ThreadLocal data such as MDC and the security context?
o: The semaphore bulkhead, which runs on the caller's thread
v.w: A thread-pool bulkhead hops threads, so context must be propagated.

v.q: What does a full semaphore bulkhead do by default?
o: Rejects the call at once with BulkheadFullException
v.w: maxWaitDuration defaults to zero.

v.q: Why does @TimeLimiter not stop a blocking method on the calling thread?
o: It works on asynchronous types and cannot interrupt a blocking call
It only works in the test profile
It requires the circuit breaker to be open
It only works with the rate limiter
v.w: Use the HTTP client's own connect and read timeouts for blocking code.

v.q: What can a TimeLimiter do when the time runs out?
o: Throw TimeoutException and cancel the running future
Retry the call on a new thread
v.w: cancelRunningFuture controls the cancel.

v.q: A rate limiter allows 50 calls per second and you run 10 pods. What is the real limit?
o: About 500 per second, because each instance has its own limiter
v.w: A fleet-wide limit needs a gateway or a distributed limiter.

v.q: Which exception signals that a rate limit was exceeded?
v.w: Each decorator has its own rejection exception.

v.q: A method calls another @CircuitBreaker method of the same class and the breaker never applies. Why?
o: The call bypasses the Spring AOP proxy (self-invocation)
Circuit breakers only work on interfaces
v.w: Move the protected call to another bean, or use the programmatic API.

v.q: What else stops the annotations from working?
o: The bean being created with new instead of by Spring
v.w: Only calls through the proxy are advised.

v.q: What does a fallback method signature look like?
o: Same return type and parameters as the protected method, plus the exception as the last parameter
A void method that logs the error
v.w: The most specific matching exception type wins.

v.q: What should a fallback return?
o: A safe result such as a conservative default or cached value
An optimistic default that looks like success
v.w: An optimistic default presents wrong data as right.

v.q: Which Actuator endpoint shows the state of circuit breakers?
v.w: Also /actuator/circuitbreakerevents, and a health indicator when registered.

v.q: Which signal is the best early alert for a struggling dependency?
o: An open breaker or a rising count of not-permitted calls
v.w: Also watch fallback rates and slow-call rates.

v.q: The client, the gateway and the service each retry three times. What is the worst case for one request?
v.w: Retry at one layer, and keep the total within the caller's deadline.

v.q: Where should you usually retry?
o: At one layer, close to the call, with backoff and jitter
At every layer to be safe
v.w: Other layers should fail fast.
